subject: SLO gating: decision worksheet & ops handoff
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@brightmart.com>, BrightMart SRE <sre@brightmart.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: SLO gating: decision worksheet & ops handoff

Hi Alex / SRE team,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — appreciated the deep dive into your streaming use case. As promised, attaching the SLO Decision Worksheet we discussed so we can lock acceptance criteria ahead of a canary. High level capture below (please flag anything missing):

- Latency: p95 server-side generation <= 350ms for 512-token prompts; first-token streaming delivered to client within 120ms of request for interactive flows.
- Throughput / concurrency: baseline sustained throughput target of 120 concurrent QPS (90th percentile across region); burst tolerance to 300 QPS for 30s windows.
- Streaming requirements: partial tokens must be available for UI within 100ms of model emitting first token; connection keepalive and chunking preferred.
- Accuracy guardrails: output sampling, temperature locked to 0.6 in canary; simple eval suite of 250 prompt samples (attached).
- Canary success thresholds: no more than 1% rate of 5xx errors, p95 latency regression < 15% vs baseline, memory/KV cache growth bounded per-session.

Attachments included: slo_acceptance_matrix.xlsx, canary_run_template.md, latency-banding-sample.json. I also created a placeholder Jira for the ops handoff: INF-4923 (see link).

Next steps (proposed):
1) BrightMart to confirm or adjust the gating numbers above by EOD Monday (Nov 30).
2) Redwood to run an initial perf validation against a synthetic workload on a mirrored dataset (2–3 days).
3) Schedule a 2-week canary window with 5% traffic and rollback policy, then iterate.
4) Procurement: we will share a scoped quote + DocuSign link for the Dedicated/reserved pool if gating passes.

If that reads OK I’ll loop in Engineering for the validation run and share run timing.

Thanks,
Vivek
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slo_acceptance_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: canary_run_template.md (markdown)]
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@brightmart.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightMart SRE <sre@brightmart.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLO gating: decision worksheet & ops handoff

Vivek — thanks for the clear summary and the artifacts. A few clarifying questions from our SRE lead before we lock numbers: 

1) Burst behavior: can your runtime guarantee prioritized low-latency paths for streaming (i.e., can requests in streaming mode be scheduled with higher priority vs batch jobs)? We need to understand preemption and queueing.
2) Cost estimate for the canary: with 5% traffic to dedicated pool for 2 weeks, what’s the expected delta vs our current on-demand spend? Rough order of magnitude is fine.
3) What observability hooks do you need from our side (headers, user/session ids) to correlate traces?

We’ll review the spreadsheet and suggest any small tweaks. Our timeline: procurement needs a decision by Dec 10th to hit Q1 rollout. Can we ensure the perf validation + canary plan completes in that window?

—Alex
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightMart
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@brightmart.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLO gating: decision worksheet & ops handoff

Alex — good questions. Short answers and operational notes below: 

1) Priority + preemption: yes. Our smart routing supports priority tagging for streaming sessions. For a dedicated pool we can reserve a concurrency band and apply soft preemption for background/long-run batch jobs. That guarantees sub-150ms variance for first-token under normal load. We’ll document exact queueing behavior in the runbook.

2) Canary cost delta: ballpark — for your expected traffic profile, a 5% canary on a Dedicated n1-standard GPU pool (multi-node) is roughly +$8k–$12k over two weeks compared to your current on-demand baseline (this assumes a mixed quantization profile). We’ll provide a detailed estimate after we capture your typical token mix and average sequence length.

3) Observability hooks: we only need a correlation id header (x-bm-cid) and optional session id. We can ingest OpenTelemetry traces if you forward spans; otherwise request-level logs with request_id + timestamp are sufficient.

Operational next steps I’ll own:
- Open INF-4923 with the runbook and sample Jenkins job.
- Schedule perf validation: target start Mon Dec 1, duration 48–72h.
- Share concrete canary schedule by Dec 3rd.

I’ve attached a small sample run configuration (canary_run_template.md) with the exact headers we expect. If you’re fine with the cost range, I’ll ask our finance team to draft the scoped quote and DocuSign envelope.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: canary_run_template.md (markdown)]
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@brightmart.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 13:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLO gating: decision worksheet & ops handoff

Quick technical note from runtime side:

- For your throughput target I recommend enabling 8-bit quantization for non-critical models during the canary; it reduces memory pressure and increases burst capacity without a noticeable quality drop for classification/short-response prompts.
- We’ll instrument KV-cache eviction thresholds per-session to avoid tail latency spikes; suggested eviction threshold is 2048 tokens/session for your workload mix.
- If you can share a sample of your 50 heaviest prompts, we can pre-warm KV caches and simulate realistic memory growth in the validation run.

Happy to jump on a 30m tech sync if helpful.

—Aditya
Senior Applied ML Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@brightmart.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLO gating: decision worksheet & ops handoff

Thanks team — that all looks reasonable. Action items from BrightMart side:

- We’ll confirm the gating numbers in the attached sheet by Mon Nov 30 EOD.
- SRE will extract the top 50 prompts and share a sanitized sample by Nov 30.
- We accept the proposed telemetry headers (x-bm-cid + session_id).
- Procurement is on the Dec 10 timeline; please ensure quote + DocuSign link are ready by Dec 3 so we can review internally.

Happy to run the 30m tech sync Monday afternoon if you’ve availability — propose Mon Dec 1, 1400 PT.

Alex
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightMart
